title: First music at home: guitar, Victrola records and Ellington outside a tavern
summary: He remembers his mother's and uncle's guitar, early records including a Massenet violin solo, and hearing Ellington's "Black and Tan Fantasy" that made him want to be a musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Was there music in your home?

My mother used to fool with the guitar, and my uncle played Blues on the guitar and sing the Blues. But my earliest recollection of hearing sound was an old Victrola or gramophone, whichever it was called, and this particular piece sticks in my mind. They had a lot of Bert Williams records and Paul Whiteman records. And I remember one thing that caught me was a violin solo, (?) Meditation, I think by Massenet. I guess I must have been no more than three years old when this captured me, and I used to sit and listen to this all day.

So in later years in Atlantic City when I was going to school, I remember one day standing outside of a tavern and hearing "Black and Tan Fantasy" (I didn't know who it was at the time, but naturally later I found it was Duke Ellington) and the "East Toodle-Oo," and I think that's what really turned me on to be a musician.
